title: stream-synchronizer-delimiter-realign-and-event-watermarks
author: Elena Park
description:
Background and motivation: we continue to see production cases where SSE fragments carrying partial JSON payloads interleave with heartbeat or tooling events and the existing delimiter heuristics misattribute trailing bytes, causing downstream JSON parse errors or function-call boundary loss. This PR introduces a stream synchronizer that (1) assigns per-connection event watermarks to detect sequence discontinuities, (2) realigns split delimiter-like byte sequences using a small rolling buffer, and (3) introduces an optional boundary-escape token to guarantee delimiter disambiguation for edge-case payloads. The change is conservative and feature-flagged so we can toggle behavior during rollout.

What this PR does: - New package: services/api/streaming/synchronizer.go implements a lightweight state machine for per-connection reassembly using watermarks and a rolling tail buffer. - SSE adapter updates: adapters/openai/sse_adapter.go uses the synchronizer to reframe incoming fragments before the JSON reassembler runs; this decouples framing concerns from JSON parsing. - SDK adjustments: sdk/ts/streaming-client.ts adapts the client-side stream parser to be tolerant of the escape token and to emit a new metadata field (event_index) used by observability. - Tests: services/api/streaming/synchronizer_test.go adds targeted unit tests for out-of-order fragments, partial-delimiter scenarios, and stress path for high-frequency heartbeat interleaving. - Docs: docs/compat/streaming-boundary.md documents the escape token format, the feature-flag, and rollout guidance for customers migrating from older streaming behavior. - Changelog entry and small CI script additions for a fuzz harness used in nightly e2e runs.

Compatibility and rollout: - Default behavior is backward compatible: the synchronizer is enabled under feature flag rts.stream_synchronizer=true. When disabled, the system behaves exactly as before. - The escape token is optional; existing clients do not need to emit it. When used, it removes ambiguity for binary or text payloads that include delimiter-like sequences. - Observability: new metrics (stream.sync.realigns, stream.sync.replay_needed, stream.sync.watermark_gaps) and a new event_index property are emitted for debugging.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover 98% of the synchronizer logic paths. - Integration tests run the adapter + runtime on a mini-cluster with a fuzz harness that replays truncated/merged fragments; CI showed an initial non-deterministic failure in e2e which was fixed by tightening the flush window. - Performance impact is negligible: the synchronizer keeps per-connection memory bounded (rolling buffer < 512 bytes) and adds a small CPU cost only during misaligned fragment events.

Checklist: - [x] Implement synchronizer and adapter integration - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add docs and changelog - [x] Feature-flag gating - [x] Observability hooks - [x] E2E fuzz harness and CI green

Related: ENG-4021 (stream stability epic), ENG-4072 (openai-compat adapter improvements). Links: internal runbook: https://linear.internal/ENG-4021, design doc: https://docs.internal/streaming-sync-design (internal).

review_threads:
Ravi Mehta: please add a comment on memory bounds for long-lived connections.
Author (Elena Park): added a bounded rolling buffer with a hard cap of 512 bytes and a circuit that triggers a replay if accumulated fragments exceed 4KB without a delimiter (tunable via config).
Sofia Alvarez: can we avoid changing the public SDK contract? The added event_index could break some downstream consumers.
Author: event_index is emitted as optional metadata; existing payloads remain unchanged. Updated SDK docs to emphasize optionality.
Jordan Liu: observed one e2e failure where heartbeat burst caused a false-positive replay.
Author: tightened the flush window and added a debounce so short bursts don't force replay. Added new unit test to assert stability under heartbeat bursts.
Ravi Mehta: CI looks good; approve after addressing minor linter note.
Sofia Alvarez: approving.
Merge: squash and merge after approvals.
ci_checks: e2e-fuzz-nightly: added (passes locally, scheduled in CI)
release_notes: Improve SSE streaming resilience by adding a stream synchronizer that realigns split delimiters and uses per-connection watermarks to detect/recover from fragment gaps. Feature-flagged rollout and optional escape token for unambiguous boundaries. Observability metrics added for relalign and replay events.
notes_for_ops: Enable rts.stream_synchronizer feature-flag in canary region first. Monitor stream.sync.replay_needed and stream.sync.watermark_gaps; threshold for rollback if replay rate > 0.1% of streaming requests for 10m. If customers rely on previous behavior, set flag to false or enable escape token on client side when possible.
backcompat_instructions: No client changes required. Optional: use escape token to guarantee delimiter boundaries for payloads that contain delimiter-like sequences. Feature is opt-in via runtime flag while we complete a staged rollout.
